incident-bot: ALERT: rate-limit spike detected for tenant=bor-eu-01 in dedicated pool=dedicated-pool-eu-west-2-borealis — 429 rate rose from 0.2% -> 18% over 5m, P50 latency stable. paging oncall: @alice.

Alice Chen: I’m on it. Pulling logs, paging Mateo for eng actions and Priya for AM/customer comms.

Mateo Rivera: seeing repeated `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` in front proxy logs tied to tenant_id=bor-eu-01. Requests per minute jumped x8 from baseline. No other tenants on this GPU pool are showing similar 429s.

Priya Nair: looping in Jordan (customer success) to confirm customer activity. Jordan, anything scheduled on your end?

Jordan Patel: customer is doing a big import this morning, but they said they'd go through our ingestion rate. They didn’t expect sustained bursts. Asking them to pause while we triage.

Alice Chen: this looks tenant-specific, likely quota enforcement kicking in on dedicated. Isolation suggests quota config or client misbehaving. Mateo, can we confirm whether token quotas or per-minute window enforcement triggered?

Mateo Rivera: checking quota logs... yes, `quota_enforcer` returned `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` for bor-eu-01 at 1721234520 onwards. Config shows soft_rate=500rpm, hard_rate=1200rpm (contract). Suddenly client traffic hit ~3800rpm.

Alice Chen: Contract hard_rate is 1200rpm — this is >2.5x. We need emergency lift or throttled fallback. Priya, do we have authorization to apply temporary override for this tenant?

Priya Nair: customer on an enterprise contract. I have contextual approval from account exec by DM but need legal/ops acknowledgement for temporary override. Leah, can you approve an emergency override for 2 hours to stabilize? We'll document post-incident.

Leah Wong: I approve an emergency quota override for borealis (bor-eu-01) for up to 2 hours. Conditions: observable rollback plan and post-mortem.

incident-bot: APPROVAL recorded: approver=Leah Wong, action=quota-override-approve, expires_in=2h.

Mateo Rivera: preparing to apply override. Proposed command: ```
# temp quota bump for tenant
redwood admin quota-override --tenant bor-eu-01 --rpm 4000 --expires 2h --reason "emergency lift: unexpected import spike"
```

Alice Chen: Before executing: confirm isolation — this dedicated pool contains only Borealis and two low-traffic tenants (svc-monitoring, test-qa). If we raise to 4k rpm ensure svc-monitoring/test-qa still respects own quotas. Mateo, will KV cache / batching pressure rise? Any memory risk on GPU nodes?

Mateo Rivera: GPU memory unaffected by request rate; throughput pressure is CPU/proxy side. Pool autoscaler will not spin up extra GPUs for dedicated (reserved) — but we have headroom on the proxies. I’ll ramp in two steps: 1200 -> 2200 -> 4000 with 2m observation windows.

deploy-bot: NOTICE: running quota-override playbook for tenant bor-eu-01 (run_id=rv-20260315-01).

Mateo Rivera: Executing step 1 -> ```redwood admin quota-override --tenant bor-eu-01 --rpm 2200 --expires 2h --run-id rv-20260315-01```

Alice Chen: Monitoring metrics: 429 rate dropped from 18% -> 9% (2m), overall token throughput increased. No cross-tenant latency impact seen on p50/p95 for other tenants.

Priya Nair: Customer confirms they lowered parallelism in client after we asked to pause, but still have backlog. They asked if we can keep higher limit short-term; we have Leah OK for 2 hours. We'll coordinate on next steps after traffic normalizes.

Mateo Rivera: Executing step 2 -> bump to 4000 rpm. Command executed. Logs: `quota_enforcer: tenant=bor-eu-01 limit=4000 applied by=mateo run_id=rv-20260315-01`.

Alice Chen: Post-bump: 429s down to 0.6% in the last 3m. p95 latency increased +20ms but within SLO. No errors in GPU runtime. Rolling monitoring window green.

incident-bot: ACTION: quota-override applied. Details: tenant=bor-eu-01, old_hard=1200, new_temporary=4000, expires_at=172123 FILL. (Note: expiration recorded in ops audit.)

Priya Nair: Will schedule a follow-up with legal and customer to formalize contract amendment for sustained higher throughput. Jordan to own customer comms.

Jordan Patel: Replied to customer: "We've applied a short-term increase to help finish your import. We'll follow up on next steps and any billing/contract updates." They replied :thumbsup:.

Alice Chen: next steps: 1) Monitor until expiry and plan graceful rollback at T-10m warning. 2) Run post-incident root cause: why client spiked and why client-side backpressure failed. 3) Update playbook to include two-step ramp and required ops approver.

Leah Wong: +1 on postmortem. Make sure to include timeline and contract action items.

Mateo Rivera: Captured short logs snippet for postmortem: ```
1721234521 GET /v1/generate 200 120ms tenant=bor-eu-01 tokens=850
1721234522 POST /v1/generate 429 8ms tenant=bor-eu-01 tokens=120
1721234523 POST /v1/generate 429 6ms tenant=bor-eu-01 tokens=130
1721234540 POST /v1/generate 200 140ms tenant=bor-eu-01 tokens=1024
```

Alice Chen: Closing note: mitigation successful, emergency lift authorized and applied, customer notified. Assign postmortem owners: Mateo (technical RCA), Priya (contract/customer), Jordan (customer side comms). I'll mark incident as mitigated and monitor until override expiry.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. If 429 rate rises above 5% again, page oncall immediately.

Priya Nair: Thanks all. Logging a follow-up with Legal and Billing for any contract amendments.

Alice Chen: Thanks team — will update the incident board and create a brief summary for execs.

Jordan Patel: Customer sent a screenshot: import finished. They said "thank you for the quick help". :tada:
